name: Ohio
tagline: Lake Erie islands, Amish hill farms, canal towns and the long Ohio River road.
intro: Ohio's byways follow the Lake Erie shore and the whole Ohio River, the old canals and the National and Lincoln roads, and wander through Amish farm country, the sandstone gorges of the Hocking Hills and the Welsh and Quaker settlements of the south. This chapter follows the 27 Ohio Byways designated by the Ohio Department of Transportation, six of which are also America's Byways. Several older state byways have since been folded into longer routes or dropped, so a few names in older guides no longer appear, and the Wayne National Forest's covered bridge road is listed separately.

members.name: Amish Country Byway
members.blurb: Back roads through Holmes County, where the Amish make up half the population, past hay wagons, a covered bridge at Walnut Creek, cheese houses and the weekly livestock auction at Mt. Hope.

members.name: Appalachian Byway
members.blurb: State Route 78 climbs from the Ohio River at Clarington into the hill country, past the bucket of the Big Muskie dragline on reclaimed mine land, and ends on Nelsonville's square of locally made brick.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Big Darby Plains Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Country roads follow Big Darby Creek across Union County's old prairie, through covered bridges built by Reuben Partridge and past pioneer graveyards where royal catchfly blooms red in late summer.

members.name: Drovers' Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The old cattle-driving road runs from Hendrysburg through Barnesville to the Great Stone Viaduct at Bellaire, past drovers' farmsteads and a stand of oaks three or four centuries old.

members.name: Granville Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short run through Granville and its township, past an inn of 1812, a Greek Revival church, Denison's chapel on College Hill and an ancient effigy mound known as the Alligator.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Heritage Corridors of Bath
members.blurb: Winding roads in Bath Township between old hamlets, past a woolen mill of 1832, an octagonal bee house, one-room schools and the living-history farm at Hale on the edge of the Cuyahoga valley.

members.name: Historic National Road
members.blurb: US 40 crosses Ohio on the line of the old National Road, through brick pike towns and past stone S bridges of 1828, the Red Brick Tavern at Lafayette and the Madonna of the Trail.

members.name: Hocking Hills Scenic Byway
members.blurb: State Route 374 winds through state forest and gorges cut in Blackhand sandstone, from Ash Cave's horseshoe rim and thin waterfall past Conkle's Hollow and Rock House to the cliffs at Cantwell.

members.name: Jefferson Township Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A pocket of country roads on Columbus's east side, along Blacklick Creek past a toll keeper's house of 1832, horse farms, family cemeteries and old barns among the new subdivisions.

members.name: Johnny Appleseed Historic Byway
members.blurb: State Route 39 and its side roads trace John Chapman's footsteps between Loudonville and Mansfield, past land he leased for apple trees, the Copus monument of 1882 and Louis Bromfield's Malabar Farm.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lake Erie Coastal Ohio Trail
members.blurb: The whole Ohio shore of Lake Erie, from Conneaut and the Ashtabula harbor light through Cleveland and Sandusky to the marshes at Magee, with ferries out to Kelleys Island and its glacial grooves.

members.name: Land of the Cross-Tipped Churches
members.blurb: Flat farm country in western Ohio where every few miles a brick church spire with a gold cross rises over the fields, from Fort Loramie's 200-foot tower to the relic shrine at Maria Stein.

members.name: Lincoln Highway Historic Byway
members.blurb: Ohio's piece of the first coast-to-coast highway, from the potteries of East Liverpool past brick road fragments near Canton, courthouse towns and Lincoln Highway pillars to Van Wert.

members.name: Lower Valley Pike Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Lower Valley Pike shadows the Mad River below limestone cliffs and past wetlands, a hand-cut stone farmhouse begun in 1825 and the Shawnee village site of Peckuwe, where a battle was fought in 1780.

members.name: Maumee Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Riverside roads down both banks of the Maumee from Defiance to Rossford, past canal locks, a mule-drawn canal boat at Providence, old river towns and the earthworks of Fort Meigs.

members.name: Miami & Erie Canal Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The byway shadows the old canal north from Piqua through German farm towns like Minster and New Bremen, past the stone lift locks at Lockington, a lockkeeper's house and the feeder lake at St. Marys.

members.name: Neil Armstrong Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short loop through Wapakoneta along the 1969 parade route, past the museum built like a moon base and the site of the old Port Koneta field, where Neil Armstrong earned his pilot certificate at 16.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: North Ridge Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Detroit Road runs along an old Lake Erie beach ridge through Avon and Sheffield, lined with more than a hundred old houses, a few surviving greenhouses and a stone house nicknamed the Stone Eagle.

members.name: Ohio & Erie Canalway
members.blurb: From Cleveland down the Cuyahoga valley along the old canal to Akron's Cascade Locks, the mule-drawn boat at Canal Fulton and the village of Zoar, ending at New Philadelphia.

members.name: Ohio River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The river road follows the Ohio for its whole length past the state, from the potteries of East Liverpool by the Fly ferry to Portsmouth's floodwall murals and Ripley's Rankin House.

members.name: Old Mill Stream Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Blanchard River's meandering course through flat farmland, from Findlay's riverside parks and the site of the Great Karg gas well to a truss bridge at Gilboa and Ottawa's brick Third Street.

members.name: Quaker Heritage Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop between Waynesville and Wilmington through Quaker farm country, past brick meetinghouses with two doors, Harvey and Hadley family houses along Todd's Fork and the fossil beds at Caesar Creek.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Scenic Olentangy Heritage Corridor
members.blurb: State Route 315 keeps to the Olentangy's west bank north of Columbus, past old stone houses, the Bieber Mill and the hundred-foot shale bluff at Highbanks.

members.name: Scioto Heritage Trail
members.blurb: Out of Portsmouth into the folded hills of Shawnee State Forest, past forest lakes, the 1874 Otway covered bridge and the Duck Run country where Roy Rogers grew up.

members.name: Tappan-Moravian Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Ridge roads around Tappan and Clendening lakes, where churches were moved uphill ahead of the water, with a loop north through Scio and Jewett to Custer's birthplace at New Rumley.

members.name: Wally Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A narrow road on an old railroad grade beside the Mohican River below Loudonville, past canoe liveries, river campgrounds, a restored one-room school and the old rail hamlet of Greer.

members.name: Welsh Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Hill roads between Gallipolis and Jackson past small Welsh chapels with two front doors, hilltop graveyards and the stone stacks of old charcoal iron furnaces such as Buckeye.

members.name: Covered Bridge Scenic Byway
members.blurb: State Route 26 follows the Little Muskingum up from Marietta through the Wayne National Forest, with ten marked tour stops and four campgrounds by the water on the way to Woodsfield.
